name: Mountain Pose
hero_alt: Mountain Pose, seen from the side
meta_description: Leaning off vertical, head drifting forward of your shoulders, neck craning? Two things usually hold back Mountain Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
og_description: Two things usually hold back Mountain Pose, and a daily exercise that fixes each one.
lede: Standing tall, shoulders over hips, ears over shoulders, weight centered through both feet. Here’s the rubric Posewise measures it against, and what to train when you miss.
rubric_intro: Posewise checks three things from the side. Here’s what good looks like.

fixes.outcome: you’ll stand tall, shoulders stacked over your hips.
fixes.why: A lean usually means the trunk isn’t holding itself up, or your weight has drifted into your heels or toes.
fixes.cue: Stack your shoulders over your hips, weight centered through your feet.

fixes.outcome: your head will stack over your shoulders.
fixes.why: A forward head is a common desk-posture pattern. It usually points to a stiff upper back and neck, not to the pose.
fixes.cue: Draw your chin back gently and lift through the crown of your head.

faq.q: Should my feet be together in Mountain Pose?
faq.a: Either way works. Big toes touching is traditional; hip-width apart is steadier if you wobble.

faq.q: Where should my weight be in Mountain Pose?
faq.a: Spread evenly across both feet, between the heels and the balls of the feet, not sinking back into your heels.

faq.q: Should I tuck my tailbone in Mountain Pose?
faq.a: Not hard. Keep the natural curve in your low back with your pelvis level, and let your ribs sit over your hips.

faq.q: What do I do with my arms in Mountain Pose?
faq.a: Let them hang relaxed by your sides, palms in or facing forward, with your shoulders soft and away from your ears.

faq.q: How can I check my Mountain Pose form at home?
faq.a: Film yourself from the side. Or use Posewise, an iPhone app that measures your Mountain Pose with the camera, speaks corrections as you hold it, and builds a six-minute daily plan for what it finds.

llms_summary: the two things that usually hold back Mountain Pose (core control for an upright, stacked torso, and a stiff upper back and neck pushing the head forward), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
